principles: Do not optimize or expand policy arbitrarily.
Keep CLI package version semantics consistent and host-neutral.
drivers: DONE output must not contradict visible repository code changes.
CLI version bumping should remain tied to watched runtime inputs unless a separate policy story changes that.
The fix should be small enough to review and test quickly.

options.name: A: Correct wording and docs only within current runtime-input policy
pros: Fixes the real user confusion exposed by B-63ba
Small, testable, and low blast radius
cons: Does not create a product-wide artifact versioning model

options.name: B: Expand CLI patch bump to experiments/** and all executable repo code
pros: Every executable code change would visibly increment the CLI version
cons: Conflates CLI runtime version with research harness changes
Changes policy beyond the reported bug

options.name: C: Add a separate experiment/product ledger now
pros: Could model non-runtime capability changes separately
cons: Too broad for this wording bug
Requires new policy and gates not requested here

chosen: A: Correct wording and docs only within current runtime-input policy
rationale: Choose A because the actual correctness issue is misleading DONE wording, not proven wrong CLI version semantics. This keeps logic consistent: package version tracks watched runtime inputs, while terminal/docs honestly explain why non-runtime code changes skip that bump.
